title: Credentialed Tier Mediator: quota-pressure aware routing and regional affinity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a new Tier Mediator component in the request router that makes per-request admission and routing decisions using: (1) credential-derived plan (free/paid/enterprise), (2) tenant token-credit pressure, (3) region affinity and latency SLOs, and (4) model-variant fallback rules (quantized/cheap models) when capacity or quota constraints apply. The goal is to reduce paid-plan latency regressions during cross-plan bursts while providing predictable graceful degradation for free-tier traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Tier Mediator service accepts upstream request metadata (credential, region hint, model preference) and returns deterministic routing decision (target model id, region, admission outcome) within 500us p50 in perf bench
Requests for enterprise tenants must not be demoted to lower plan lanes unless explicit spill policy threshold is reached; verified by integration tests and canary traffic
Free-tier requests should be demoted to cheap quantized variants when tenant credit falls below configured pressure threshold, with audit log entries for every demotion
Regional affinity honored: if primary region has no capacity, Tier Mediator attempts same-cloud fallback region within same geo before global fallback; verified by simulation harness
Rolling canary (10% -> 30% -> 100%) completes with no regressions in runtime-1.21 baseline dashboards (latency P95, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization)
Unit and e2e tests cover: score computation, fairness window, forced spillback, quota-refill edge cases, and audit logging format
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight 'tier_score' function: tier_score = base_priority + alpha * credit_ratio - beta * estimated_latency_delta; alpha/beta configurable via flags
Maintain per-tenant leaky-window creditsummary in Redis (60s sliding) for pressure heuristics; fallback to token service on cache miss

Admission policy flow: compute tier_score -> if above 'fastpath_threshold' route to fast lane in same region; else if above 'slowpath_threshold' route to lower-cost instance or alternate region; else return soft-degrade (HTTP 429 with 'retry-after' or best-effort cheap model)

Model variant mapping: primary_model -> [full_fp16, int8_variant, trimmed-sequence_optimized] with compatibility table in config store; mediator chooses variant that satisfies model-compatibility and quota target
Integrate audit events into existing eventstream (topic: routing.audit.v2) with fields: request_id, tenant_id, original_plan, chosen_plan, reason_code, decision_path
Expose feature flags for live tuning: enable_quota_pressure, enable_regional_spill, fastpath_threshold, slowpath_threshold, fairness_window_seconds
rollout_plan: Local dev: unit tests + mock token service (done)
Staging: enable Tier Mediator for internal tenants only; run 24h soak with synthetic burst tests
Canary-1: 10% traffic (non-critical endpoints) for 6h; monitor churn and errors
Canary-2: 30% traffic for 24h; run perf benchmarks and A/B compare with control group
Full rollout: 100% after stability gates; enable audit sampling at 100% and start cost evaluation
Rollback: feature flags to instantly disable mediator; emergency kill switch in router config and runbook documented
risks_and_mitigations: Starvation risk: free-plan starvation if thresholds too aggressive -> mitigation: min-serve-gamma that guarantees X requests/min per plan and backlog smoothing
Priority inversion: an enterprise tenant with bursty low-credit pattern could be demoted incorrectly -> mitigation: enterprise_exempt flag and soft_grace_window that delays demotion for 30s
Telemetry lag: false positives in quota pressure due to delayed metrics -> mitigation: conservative smoothing and fallback to token service authoritative read
Operational complexity: new knobs increase cognitive load for SRE -> mitigation: sane defaults, one-click playbooks and a 'safe-mode' that automates thresholds based on historical traffic
Audit/log volume: high audit event rate -> mitigation: sample free-tier demotion events at 10% by default, full audit for enterprise
